Witness links two 'Razakars'
2016-09-21T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/city/witness-links-two-razakars-1287217

The 13th prosecution witness in a case against two alleged Kishoreganj Razakars yesterday linked them to the killing of a fellow freedom fighter, saying the victim's wife narrated it to him and some others that very day during the 1971 Liberation War.

Facing six charges, Syed Mohammad Hussain alias Hossain is on the run while Muhammad Moslem Pradhan pleads not guilty in jail.

Gopal Chandra Das, from Mohammadpur (previously known as Keshobpur) under Nikli upazila, told International Crimes Tribunal-1 that he was a member of Cobra Bahini and took part in several battles against Razakar Bahini around Bangladesh.

The 67-year-old said their commander Motiur Rahman led them in an attack on the auxiliary force of the Pakistani occupation army near Nikli sadar on the morning of October 19.

Hussain, commander of Nikli Thana unit of Razakars, and Moslem, commander of Nikli sadar union unit of Razakars, launched a counter attack and the freedom fighters retreated as part of their strategy, he said.

In the afternoon, a fellow fighter Abdul Malek went to his house and they heard gunshots around 5:30pm, said Gopal. They came to know that Malek was shot dead near one Debendra Chandra Nath's home in Purbagram, he said.

On reaching Malek's house, the victim's wife Rabeya Khatun told them that Moslem had shot Malek dead on forcibly taking him away with other Razakars saying it had been instructed by Hussain, said Gopal.

The three-member tribunal led by Justice Anwarul Haque adjourned proceedings until today after the defence completed Gopal's cross-examination.
